label: ikanimo
title: いかにも
meaning_example: the bag indeed looks heavy, but its empty

notes.text:
Description + いかにも + evidence to the contrary = seems (but isn't)

Desciption + いかにも = indeed
notes.html:
Description + いかにも + evidence to the contrary = seems (but isn't)
Desciption + いかにも = indeed

examples.japanese: あのかばんはいかにも重そうだが、中身はからで、１キロしかない。
examples.body_text:
あのかばんはいかにも重そうだが、中身はからで、１キロしかない。 

		The bag 
		indeed looks 
		heavy, but there's nothing inside, so it only weighs 1 kilo.
examples.body_html:
あのかばんはいかにも重そうだが、中身はからで、１キロしかない。 
The bag indeed looks heavy, but there's nothing inside, so it only weighs 1 kilo.

comments.text: In #, if you want to say 親切な, you have to say "kind," but if you say 優しい then you can say "gentle." YOu can be 親切 but do not necessarily be 優しい and vice versa.
comments.html: In #, if you want to say 親切な, you have to say "kind," but if you say 優しい then you can say "gentle." YOu can be 親切 but do not necessarily be 優しい and vice versa.

優しい　【やさしい】gentle

comments.text: It is true that 親切な and 優しい are often mixed up. However, technically speaking 親切 is what is represented by the act of Good Samaritan in the Bible, meaning going out of one's way to help, but this does not necessrily mean he is 優しい, which means that he is gentle of disposition and sweet-tempered. A sweet-tempered person could often be a kind person at the same time, but that is not the necessary condition.
